events.title: FOMC hikes 25 bp to 3.75–4.00%
events.why_it_matters: Unanimous first hike since 2023, with the median 2026 dot at 4.1%, re-anchors equities, credit, housing, and the dollar to a possible second hike.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 7 minutes for 25 vs 50 bp debate and the conditions for another move at the Oct 27–28 meeting (no SEP).

events.title: White House memo to restrict Canadian goods in U.S. federal procurement
events.why_it_matters: Directs OMB/USTR to identify and, where lawful, remove Canadian-origin items from federal civil procurement in retaliation for Buy Canadian barriers in a WTO GPA market the White House pegs above $280 billion.
events.what_to_watch: FAR/OMB implementation lists and any Canadian federal or provincial countermeasures.

events.title: EDVA unseals Google ad-tech remedies (behavioral, no breakup)
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected AdX divestiture but ordered a six-year worldwide interoperability, data-sharing, and AdWords non-discrimination decree with a monitor—material for GOOGL and the open-web ad stack.
events.what_to_watch: Joint proposed final judgment due Oct 2 and whether DOJ appeals the no-breakup outcome.

events.title: BOJ hikes policy rate 25 bp to 1.25%
events.why_it_matters: 7-2 hike to a 31-year high, with Ueda leaving the door open to consecutive or larger moves as energy and AI demand broaden inflation—yen and global carry are live.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 29–30 Outlook meeting (outside this window) and any yen spike that tightens global financial conditions before then.

events.title: H-1B $100,000 entry restriction extended 12 months
events.why_it_matters: Proclamation 11069 extends the $100k H-1B payment through Sept 21, 2027 and EO 14431 tightens interagency scrutiny, but a Massachusetts district court vacatur still blocks collection of the fee.
events.what_to_watch: First Circuit appeal of the fee vacatur, DHS national-interest exceptions, and FY2027 cap/consular volumes.

events.title: Graham Act signed: up to 500% Russia tariffs and secondary energy-buyer tariffs
events.why_it_matters: P.L. 119-111 requires additional duties of up to 500% on Russian imports within ~30 days and authorizes up to 100% tariffs on all goods from top buyers of Russian oil/gas or sanctions-evasion facilitators (China/India risk).
events.what_to_watch: Presidential implementation/waivers around mid-October and whether secondary tariffs are actually aimed at China or India.

events.title: Trump–Xi Washington summit extends U.S.–China trade truce
events.why_it_matters: Leaders extended the trade truce to Jan 10, 2027, sketched a ~$30bn-each-way tariff-cut framework plus coal purchases, and deferred the near-term tariff/export-control cliff; Taiwan and tech controls were not resolved.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation of the 30-for-30 list, BIS affiliates-rule pause durability, and the next leader meetings at APEC (Nov) and G20 (Dec).

events.title: Costco Q4 FY2026 beat; IEEPA tariff-refund EPS tailwind
events.why_it_matters: Q4 EPS $6.75 and +9.4% comps confirm consumer resilience; a +$0.15 net IEEPA tariff-refund item is a live marker for how Supreme Court tariff refunds flow through retailers.
events.what_to_watch: Remaining refund cadence in FY2027 and whether peers guide similar one-time EPS.

events.title: BIS temporary rule restricts polysilicon stockpiling
events.why_it_matters: Commerce/BIS TFR under Proclamation 11052 limits importer stockpiling of polysilicon and derivatives ahead of Dec 4, 2026 Section 232 import adjustments—a supply-chain hit for solar and semiconductor inputs.
events.what_to_watch: Waiver grants, new-importer weekly caps, and the Dec 4 minimum-price/tariff details.

events.title: China mini-stimulus: State Council plus mortgage subsidy and PSL cut
events.why_it_matters: After Li Qiang's Sept 28 call for stronger counter-cyclical support, MOF/PBOC launched a 1 ppt first-home mortgage interest subsidy (effective Oct 1, 1-year trial) and cut the PSL rate 25 bp to 1.5% with larger relending quotas.
events.what_to_watch: Golden Week property transactions, special-bond/project starts, and whether LPR or RRR follow.

events.title: FTC/states settle Corteva pesticide loyalty-rebate case
events.why_it_matters: 10-year ban on share-based distributor loyalty programs plus $35 million to states should open generic crop-protection share and pressure Corteva pricing; Syngenta remains in litigation.
events.what_to_watch: Court entry of the stipulated order and any Syngenta settlement or trial date.

events.title: JOLTS job openings (August) cool to 7.079 million
events.why_it_matters: Openings fell to 7.079 million (4.3% rate) vs ~7.2–7.3 million expected, with quits still low—first labor print after the Sept 16 hike arguing the market is cooling, not breaking.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 2 payrolls and wages to confirm whether the Fed can still justify another hike.

events.title: Iran war / Strait of Hormuz oil disruption (ongoing)
events.why_it_matters: Six-month US/Israel–Iran war still constrains Hormuz flows (partial rebound toward ~7.4 mb/d Strait shipments) and keeps Brent in a roughly $100–108 range, feeding global inflation and central-bank hawkishness.
events.what_to_watch: Qatari-mediated talks after Trump rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz reopening plan; tanker rates, SPR, and any ceasefire headline.

events.title: China NBS/Caixin manufacturing PMI return to expansion
events.why_it_matters: Official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.1 (from 49.8) and Caixin to 52.1, with Reuters tying the bounce to the AI boom—first expansion print into Golden Week and after the mini-stimulus.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the rebound survives the Oct 1–7 holiday and shows up in export/property high-frequency data next week.

events.title: BEA Q2 GDP third estimate and August PCE
events.why_it_matters: Same-morning GDP (2nd estimate 1.5% annualized, plus annual-revision noise) and the Fed's preferred PCE gauge is the first inflation/growth check after the hike; consensus clusters near +0.4% headline / +0.3% core PCE m/m.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE vs 3.3% y/y, real spending, and how large the annual update revisions are.

events.title: ADP private payrolls (September)
events.why_it_matters: Private-sector ADP at 8:15 a.m. ET is the last high-frequency jobs read before Friday's NFP; August was a weak +38k.
events.what_to_watch: A sub-50k print would reinforce JOLTS cooling; a rebound would keep October hike odds alive into NFP.

events.title: FCC votes on satellite spectrum unlock and NEPA rewrite
events.why_it_matters: Open meeting (10:30 a.m. ET) would free >1,000 MHz (12.7 GHz and 42 GHz) for FSS and codify that most spectrum/space authorizations are not NEPA major federal actions, accelerating satellite broadband buildout.
events.what_to_watch: Final vote text, earth-station/space-station exclusions, and Ku/Ka/D-band FNPRMs.

events.title: Micron FY2026 Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: AI memory bellwether guided ~$50bn revenue ±$1bn and ~$31 non-GAAP EPS ±$1; print/guide will set HBM/DRAM pricing expectations across semis after the close.
events.what_to_watch: Q1 FY27 guide, HBM supply commentary, and any capex/FCF surprise vs the $10bn Q4 capex plan.

events.title: Nike Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global wholesale/consumer bellwether; consensus ~$0.44 EPS and ~$11.33bn sales (both down YoY) will signal China, inventory, and post-World-Cup demand.
events.what_to_watch: Greater China commentary, gross-margin/inventory, and any FY27 guide reset.

events.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: First real-side activity print after the hike; August manufacturing PMI was 54.6, so prices-paid and new orders will color the inflation-vs-growth debate into NFP.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs 50, prices paid, and employment sub-index.

events.title: China Golden Week market/factory shutdown
events.why_it_matters: Mainland exchanges, Stock Connect, and many factories close Oct 1–7, thinning Asia liquidity into U.S. NFP and leaving CNH as the onshore price-discovery channel.
events.what_to_watch: Holiday travel/retail prints, property transactions, and Oct 8 reopen gap after U.S. jobs.

events.title: September employment situation (NFP)
events.why_it_matters: First payrolls print after the hike; August was +162k / 4.1% U3, while Street now clusters ~84k–90k and 4.1% unemployment—a miss or wage surprise immediately reprices extra-hike odds.
events.what_to_watch: Private payrolls, AHE (~+0.3% m/m consensus), and revisions to the strong August print.

events.title: Google ad-tech joint proposed final judgment due
events.why_it_matters: Parties must file one jointly proposed Final Judgment reflecting Brinkema's behavioral decree; disputed language will show how tight interoperability and AdWords limits actually are.
events.what_to_watch: Effective-date/implementation timelines (often 60 days after entry) and any DOJ appeal signal.

events.title: OPEC+ core-seven meeting on November quotas
events.why_it_matters: After holding October output unchanged on Sept 6, delegates expect the seven (ex-UAE) to keep November quotas steady while Hormuz disruptions still cap the group's ability to add barrels.
events.what_to_watch: Any surprise cut/hike vs the hold, and 2027 baseline/quota talk.

events.title: ISM Services PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: Services are ~70% of the economy; August services PMI was 55.4, so a downshift after weak JOLTS/confidence would argue the hike is landing.
events.what_to_watch: Headline, prices paid, and employment vs manufacturing PMI.

events.title: Constellation Brands Q2 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Beer/spirits bellwether is an early read on U.S. consumer trade-down, Hispanic beer demand, and Mexico supply after a tough staples tape.
events.what_to_watch: Beer depletion/shipments, guidance, and any tariff or Mexico-production commentary.

events.title: U.S. international trade in goods and services (August)
events.why_it_matters: August goods/services balance will show whether tariff/truce dynamics and energy prices are still widening the deficit into Q3 GDP.
events.what_to_watch: Goods deficit vs China and petroleum trade after Hormuz freight spikes.

events.title: FOMC minutes of the September 15–16 hike meeting
events.why_it_matters: Three-week minutes will show how close the Committee was to 50 bp vs 25 bp and the reaction function for another hike, with no SEP at the Oct 27–28 meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Language on energy passthrough, labor tightness after JOLTS, and dissent risk even though the vote was 12-0.

events.title: PepsiCo Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Pricing-power/volume split at a mega-cap staple will test whether Costco-style consumer resilience extends to center-store after energy-driven food inflation.
events.what_to_watch: Organic volume vs price, Frito-Lay margins, and FY26 outlook.

events.title: Delta Air Lines Q3 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Airline bellwether transmits jet-fuel/Hormuz costs and premium-leisure demand into industrials; unit-cost surprises can move the whole group.
events.what_to_watch: CASM-ex, fuel hedge commentary, and Q4 capacity/guidance.

events.title: SEMICON West (San Francisco)
events.why_it_matters: First major post-Micron equipment/materials gathering; capex and HBM/advanced-packaging commentary can reprice the AI hardware complex.
events.what_to_watch: WFE order commentary, China-tool demand, and any supply-constraint talk after the polysilicon 232 rule.

events.title: Anthropic IPO marketing window (possible mid-October launch)
events.why_it_matters: Confidential S-1 (June) and late-September prospectus leaks point to a potential $2tn-class AI listing; roadshow talk for mid-October could squeeze AI-adjacent multiples even if pricing slips to November.
events.what_to_watch: Public S-1 on EDGAR, underwriter launch, and whether the deal waits for midterms/Q3 numbers.

events.title: September CPI
events.why_it_matters: Last major inflation print inside this window and a core input for the Oct 27–28 FOMC; energy from Hormuz is the swing factor after August CPI at 3.4%/2.4% core.
events.what_to_watch: Core vs energy contribution and whether services disinflation survived the oil spike.

events.title: Fed Beige Book
events.why_it_matters: Anecdotal district color on prices, wages, and demand two weeks before the October FOMC, useful if NFP/CPI conflict.
events.what_to_watch: Energy-price passthrough language and labor-shortage vs cooling comments.

top_risks: Hot August PCE / September NFP or CPI keeps a second 2026 FOMC hike fully in play into the Oct 27–28 meeting.
Iran–Hormuz re-escalation (or failed talks) sends oil back above recent $108 Brent highs and tightens global financial conditions.
Graham Act secondary tariffs aimed at top buyers of Russian energy (China/India) reopen a trade-shock channel the Trump–Xi truce just narrowed.
Micron guide miss or HBM pricing peak talk hits the AI-hardware complex into SEMICON West.
China property mini-stimulus fails to show up in Golden Week transactions, undercutting the PMI bounce.
top_opportunities: Confirmed cooling in labor (JOLTS already soft; NFP ~84–90k) lets markets fade the second-hike tail.
Hormuz de-escalation / higher Middle East loadings would drop oil and ease the global inflation impulse.
China PMI back above 50 plus mortgage subsidy/PSL is a near-term bid for China-sensitive cyclicals and materials into the holiday.
U.S.–China truce to Jan 10, 2027 plus 30-for-30 tariff cuts reduce near-term export-control/tariff cliff risk for tech and consumer goods.
FCC satellite-spectrum/NEPA streamlining is a structural positive for FSS/broadband names if the Sept 30 vote lands as drafted.
summary: The tape is still digesting a unanimous Sept 16 FOMC hike to 3.75–4.00% against an unfinished Iran/Hormuz oil shock, with today's PCE/GDP and Friday's NFP the first hard tests of whether another hike is live. A modest U.S.–China truce extension to Jan 10, 2027 and China's mortgage/PSL mini-stimulus cut near-term policy-cliff risk, but the Graham Act's secondary-tariff authorities and still-restricted Hormuz flows keep a fat left tail. Quality over drama: shutdown risk is off (CR through Dec 11), debt ceiling is a 2027 issue, and Atlantic hurricane season remains unusually quiet.
